title: the cave of Svayamprabha
hook: late, empty-handed, and tempted to hide or give up
carry: a line of monkeys on the shore

segments.voice: Yesterday: Svayamprabha led them out with eyes covered and asked nothing back. But the month was already gone.

On the beach, Angada does the math, and it's bad. They're late. They haven't found Sita. Sugriva warned that anyone who came back late would answer with their life. And Angada carries a private fear on top of that. He's Vali's son. His uncle took his father's throne with Rama's help. Angada wonders whether Sugriva has ever really trusted him. Back late and empty-handed? He decides he isn't going back at all.
screen: `ANGADA DOES THE MATH.` → `A PRIVATE FEAR.` → `HE WON'T GO BACK.`

segments.voice: Despair spreads fast. Angada tells the others he'll fast to death right here on the shore, a vow called prayopavesha, sitting down to die without food. One of the monkeys, named Tara, a different Tara from Vali's widow, offers another way out: let's go back to the cave. It has everything, food, water, safety. We could live there forever and no one could reach us. Several monkeys like the idea. Then Hanuman speaks. He sees the group about to split. To Angada he's gentle: Sugriva is fair, and you're dear to him; don't assume the worst. About the cave he's blunt: Lakshmana's arrows could split that cave open. Hiding isn't safety. And Valmiki says Hanuman quietly wins the others over, one by one, so they won't follow Angada into the cave. It doesn't fully work. Angada isn't convinced. He spreads sacred darbha grass on the shore and sits down to die, and the other monkeys sit down with him, a long line of them along the sea, waiting. They start to talk about how they got here. About Rama. About Sita. About Kaikeyi's demand, and Dasharatha's death. And about Jatayu, the old vulture who died fighting Ravana. And up on the hillside behind them, out of a cave, something very old is listening.
screen: `PRAYOPAVESHA: A FAST TO DEATH.` · `THE PULL BACK TO THE CAVE.` · `HANUMAN: HIDING ISN'T SAFETY.` · `A LINE OF MONKEYS ON THE SHORE.`

segments.voice: Notice, gently, whether there's somewhere in your life you've quietly given up, not to fix it now, just to see it. Breathe in and name it; breathe out and let one person's voice come to mind who would tell you, kindly, not to quit yet. If giving up ever feels like more than that, please reach out today: in the US, call or text 988, or your local emergency number.
Prayopavesha, sitting down to fast unto death: the vow Angada takes today on the shore, when Hanuman argues that hiding in the cave isn't safety either.
Your line: a line of monkeys on the shore. Even here, the story isn't over. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Prayopavesha, fasting unto death, appears in the epics as a solemn vow; Hindu teachers today speak of it only in very specific traditional contexts, and in the Ramayana the monkeys' vow is interrupted before it's carried out.

chat.says: When Angada wanted to give up on the shore, what did Hanuman tell him?
options: Gently: Sugriva is fair and you're dear to him, so don't assume the worst.
That hiding forever in the golden cave would keep every one of them safe.
That they should split up and each search a stretch of the coast alone.
chat.meaning: Hanuman is gentle with Angada, Sugriva is fair, don't assume the worst, and blunt about the cave: hiding isn't safety.

prayopavesha.meaning: a vow to sit and fast unto death

darbha.meaning: a sacred grass used in rites

Kaikeyi.meaning: Rama's stepmother, whose demand sent him into exile

Jatayu.meaning: the old vulture who died fighting Ravana

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda 53–55 (Angada's despair; the cave plan; Hanuman's counsel; the fast)

notes: Sarga numbers follow the common (vulgate) numbering and differ between editions; confirm against the edition the Keeper uses.
Hanuman's arguments (Sugriva is fair; Lakshmana's arrows could split the cave) and his effort to detach the others: paraphrased from Kishkindha 54; confirm.
Topics of the monkeys' talk on the shore (Kaikeyi, Dasharatha, Jatayu): confirm in Kishkindha 56.
Fasting to death is handled descriptively as the epic's vow; the practice and carry steer away from it. A Keeper should check the framing.
